title: BalatroBot on the simulator
---

# BalatroBot on the simulator

Jackdaw speaks [BalatroBot](https://github.com/coder/balatrobot) v1.5.2's JSON-RPC API on top of
its own engine. The command and view layer is a port of BalatroBot's Lua
(`crates/jackdaw-bot`, pinned to upstream commit `9052d76f14723293f6c6b2cecaa791a5c4ae68f3`;
the vendored source is in `third_party/balatrobot/v1.5.2/`), so a client written for the live
game (an agent, a script, BalatroBot's own test suite) drives the simulator unchanged, and an
agent trained on the simulator can be pointed at the live game.

What "the same API" covers:

- **Commands.** Every v1.5.2 endpoint, with the same parameters, the same argument validation
  (Lua semantics: JSON `null` is an absent field, `{}` and `[]` are both an empty table,
  "integer" means `floor(v) == v`), the same state gates and the same checks in the same order,
  with the exact error names, codes and messages.
- **The view.** `gamestate` and every endpoint that returns the game state send the structure
  `gamestate.lua` builds: the same fields, present or left out under the same conditions, empty
  tables as `[]`, numbers printed with `%.14g`.
- **Text fields carry names.** Where the live game sends a localized description (a card's
  `value.effect`, a boss blind's `effect`, a tag's `tag_effect`), the simulator sends the name.

Game rules follow vanilla Balatro 1.0.1o, as the engine does everywhere. Where BalatroBot pushes
the game past a gate a player can't (selling an eternal joker, a greyed-out pack pick), the
simulator refuses; where Steamodded changes vanilla, the difference is documented
([Where the live game isn't vanilla](live#where-the-live-game-isnt-vanilla)) rather than
imitated.

## Entry points

**`jackdaw serve`** runs BalatroBot's HTTP server on the simulator:

```bash
jackdaw serve                                   # 127.0.0.1:12346, like BalatroBot
jackdaw serve --port 0                          # any free port (printed on start)
jackdaw serve --host 0.0.0.0 --fs-root runs/    # off loopback a filesystem root is required
jackdaw serve --debug                           # also BalatroBot's test endpoints
```

**`SimBackend`** is the same session in-process (`jackdaw.bridge`). `handle(method, params)`
returns the result dict or raises `RPCError` with BalatroBot's `code`, `message` and
`data = {"name": ...}`. `add` also accepts the engine's names (`m_glass`, `foil`, `Gold`), as
`LiveBackend` does.

```python
from jackdaw.bridge import SimBackend
from jackdaw.engine.actions import PlayHand

sim = SimBackend()
sim.handle("start", {"deck": "RED", "stake": "WHITE", "seed": "TEST123"})
view = sim.handle("select", {})
sim.legal_actions()                             # BALATROBOT legality, as engine actions
sim.request_for(PlayHand(card_indices=(0, 2)))  # ("play", {"cards": [0, 2]})
```

**`jackdaw.core.Game`** (the Rust engine) has the bot layer too: `bot_view()` (the view as a
dict), `bot_request(action)` (the request that performs an action, or `None`) and
`legal_actions(Legality.BALATROBOT)`. `jackdaw._core.BotSession` is the raw session (JSON text
in and out) behind all of these.

**`LiveAdapter`** (`jackdaw.bridge`; also what `BridgeAdapter(backend)` gives) plays the
environment over the protocol, with a shadow run in the Rust engine: each request is taken by
the shadow through this layer first, then sent to the backend, and the backend's view is
compared with the shadow's `bot_view()` (`DivergenceError` on a difference). The mask and legal
actions follow BALATROBOT legality. Over `LiveBackend` that is the live game; known Steamodded
and BalatroBot differences are handled by a deviation catalog, and `jackdaw lockstep` runs it at
scale. Over `SimBackend()` it is BalatroBot's API on the simulator. See
[Lockstep against the live game](live).

## Command-space policy

The engine's action set and BalatroBot's endpoints don't line up one to one.

**Translated.** Each engine action has one request (`Game.bot_request`, Rust
`jackdaw_bot::translate`). `SortHand` and the `Swap*` actions go out as `rearrange` with the
whole permutation (a sort is the permutation that sorts the hand). The sort *mode*
(`G.hand.config.sort`) has no BalatroBot counterpart: after a translated sort by suit, cards
drawn later are still placed by rank, in the live game and in the simulator alike.

**Sim-only, masked under BALATROBOT legality.** Moves vanilla allows that the live bot can't make:

- `RerollBoss` (Director's Cut, Retcon) and `BuyAndUse` have no endpoint;
- `use` and `sell` outside `SELECTING_HAND` and `SHOP`: vanilla also lets a consumable be used
  at blind select, on the cash-out screen and in an open pack, and a card be sold at blind
  select and in an open pack;
- a consumable that takes cards (`max_highlighted`), used in the shop;
- Aura through `use`: its config has no `max_highlighted`, so `use.lua` never highlights a target
  and the card can't be used (`pack` special-cases it, so an Aura pick works);
- buying, or picking from a pack, a Negative joker at full joker slots (the bot compares the count
  with the limit and has no Negative exception);
- reordering the jokers at blind select and on the cash-out screen: vanilla's drag works at every
  decision point (`CardArea:align_cards` re-sorts the jokers by position in any state), but
  `rearrange` requires `SELECTING_HAND`, `SHOP` or `SMODS_BOOSTER_OPENED`. Inside a pack
  the two agree: the jokers, and an Arcana or Spectral pack's dealt hand, can be reordered. The
  consumables can be dragged too, and `rearrange` takes them, but no rule reads their order, so
  the engine has no move for it.

**BalatroBot allows, vanilla forbids.** The live endpoints call `G.FUNCS` directly and skip two
UI gates. The simulator keeps vanilla's rules and refuses, with `NOT_ALLOWED`:

- selling an eternal joker: `Cannot sell '<name>': the card is eternal (vanilla's sell button
  refuses it)`;
- a pack pick the game greys out (Judgement or The Soul at full joker slots, The Emperor at full
  consumable slots, ...): `Cannot select '<name>' from the pack: vanilla greys this pick out (it
  cannot be used now)` ([B01](live#b01)).

`play` and `discard` click the requested cards as BalatroBot does: under Cerulean Bell the forced
card stays highlighted and the selection stops at five, so a request that leaves the forced card
out plays what the live game plays ([B02](live#b02)). A request whose clicks end
with no card highlighted (one index given twice) is refused: vanilla never plays an empty hand.

**Debug only.** `add`, `set`, `save`, `load` and `menu` change the run in ways no move does;
they are never in a legal-action list.

**Legality.** `Legality.VANILLA` is the engine's legal list (Balatro 1.0.1o).
`Legality.BALATROBOT` keeps the vanilla actions whose request passes BalatroBot's checks: the
dispatcher's argument and state checks and the endpoint's own validation, run as a dry run that
changes nothing. Every action it allows is one the live bot accepts. From Python:
`Game.legal_actions(Legality.BALATROBOT)`, `SimBackend.legal_actions()`; from Rust:
`jackdaw_bot::legal_actions(&game, Legality::Balatrobot)` and, per action,
`jackdaw_bot::bot_accepts(&game, &action)`. A `PlayHand` / `Discard` with no cards (the legal
list's marker for "any selection") is checked with one card, the forced one if any.

## Endpoints

| method | states | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `health` | any | |
| `gamestate` | any | the view (`MENU` before a run) |
| `rpc.discover` | any | the vendored `openrpc.json` |
| `menu` | any | ends the run |
| `start` | `MENU` | random vanilla seed when none is given |
| `select`, `skip` | `BLIND_SELECT` | the Boss can't be skipped |
| `play`, `discard` | `SELECTING_HAND` | clicks as above; at most 5 cards |
| `cash_out` | `ROUND_EVAL` | |
| `buy`, `reroll`, `next_round` | `SHOP` | `buy` takes `card`, `voucher` or `pack` |
| `sell`, `use` | `SELECTING_HAND`, `SHOP` | eternal jokers refused |
| `pack` | `SMODS_BOOSTER_OPENED` | greyed picks refused |
| `rearrange` | `SELECTING_HAND`, `SHOP`, `SMODS_BOOSTER_OPENED` | the whole permutation |
| `add`, `set` | see upstream | debug |
| `save`, `load` | see upstream | snapshot files (below) |
| `screenshot` | see upstream | always `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| `test_*` | any | only with `--debug` / `debug=True` |

`use` highlights its targets the vanilla way: Cerulean Bell's forced card first, then the given
cards, a repeat skipped. BalatroBot clears the highlight with `force` first, dropping the forced
card; for the requests the legal list makes (the forced card among the targets) the two agree.

## The view

- **States.** `G.STATE`'s name, with Steamodded's `SMODS_BOOSTER_OPENED` for every open pack;
  `MENU` before the first `start` and after `menu`; `UNKNOWN` after a `load` that deleted the run
  and then failed.
- **Areas.** `jokers`, `consumables`, `cards` (the deck), `hand`, and in the shop `shop`,
  `vouchers`, `packs`; `pack` while a pack is open. Each has `count`, `limit`,
  `highlighted_limit` (5 for the hand and the deck, 1 elsewhere) and `cards`. Limits are the
  game's `card_limit`s: joker and consumable slots, the hand size, the shop's joker slots, one
  voucher slot per shop (plus one per Voucher Tag), two booster slots, the pack's size, and the
  deck's limit (52, raised by an overfilling emplace, lowered to the playing-card count every
  frame, plus one for Marble Joker, Cryptid and DNA).
- **Leftover shop areas.** After the shop closes, `G.shop_jokers`, `G.shop_vouchers` and
  `G.shop_booster` still point at the removed areas: the view keeps reporting them with no cards
  and the last frame's count, until the run ends (read from the code, not yet captured live).
- **Cards.** `label` is the center's label (`Glass Card`, `Joker`, `The Fool`); playing cards
  cost 1 to buy and to sell; `modifier.enhancement` is `ability.effect` upper-cased for every
  card, so jokers and consumables report theirs (`"MULT"`, `"ENHANCE"`); flags that are false
  (`eternal`, `rental`, `debuff`, `hidden`, `highlight`) are left out, and a card with none has
  `modifier: []` / `state: []`.
- **Hands.** All twelve, secret ones included, with `example` lists.
- **Blinds.** `score` is always computed from the blind's multiplier and the ante's base amount;
  `effect`, `tag_name` and `tag_effect` carry names.
- **`used_vouchers`** maps each redeemed voucher's key to `""`.
- **JSON.** Encoded as Steamodded's rxi `json.lua` does: an empty table is `[]`, numbers are
  printed with `%.14g` (14 significant digits, exact ties to even, as the game's LuaJIT 2.0.5
  does on Windows). Object keys are not in Lua's `pairs` order (JSON objects are unordered).
- **NaN and infinity** can't be encoded. The live server then sends nothing and the client times
  out; the simulator answers `INTERNAL_ERROR` `Failed to encode response: unexpected number
  value 'inf'`. The request itself has taken effect in both.

## Save and load

`save` writes the run's canonical snapshot (`jackdaw.snapshot/1` JSON,
[snapshot-schema.md](snapshot-schema)) and `load` reads one; neither touches the game's `.jkr`
saves, so files don't move between the simulator and the live game. As in the live game, `load`
deletes the run before reading the file: a bad file leaves no run (`UNKNOWN`) until `menu` or a
good `load`. With `--fs-root` (required off loopback) every path must stay inside that
directory. The runtime-only parts of the view restart on `load`: the deck limit becomes the
playing-card count and the leftover shop areas are gone. The live game rebuilds its card areas
from the save, limits included; this difference hasn't been captured live.

## The server

`jackdaw serve` follows `server.lua`: one connection at a time, one request per connection
(`Connection: close`), `POST /` only (other methods: 405, other paths: 404), bodies up to 64 KiB.
The JSON-RPC envelope: `jsonrpc` must be `"2.0"`, `id` is required and must be an integer or a
string and is echoed back, errors carry `{code, message, data: {name}}`. Endpoint errors use
BalatroBot's names and codes: `INTERNAL_ERROR` -32000, `BAD_REQUEST` -32001, `INVALID_STATE`
-32002, `NOT_ALLOWED` -32003.

## Differences from the live game

Besides the policy above:

- **Timing.** The live endpoints answer once the game reaches the state they wait for; the
  simulator settles every request at once. A live request can hang where the simulator answers:
  `skip` with a tag that opens a pack waits for `BLIND_SELECT` live; the simulator returns the
  open pack. A live answer can also come before the game's queued events have run: `cash_out`
  answers once the shop has its cards, before a tag's shop effect (the D6 Tag's free reroll, the
  Voucher Tag's voucher, the edition tags) has run in its animated events, and the lockstep reads
  `gamestate` again until it settles (`docs/live.md`). The `play` that beats a boss can answer
  before the round evaluation's `Blind:defeat` has run (from a run's second round, below), and
  `defeat` lifts the boss's debuffs with `set_blind(nil)` in an event 0.95 × 1.3 s after it
  (`blind.lua:296-343`). That answer can still show The Manacle's lost hand size, Amber Acorn's
  face-down jokers, the cards the boss debuffed, and Crimson Heart's joker still debuffed,
  without its passive (Juggler's hand size, Drunkard's discard, Chaos the Clown's free
  reroll); the next answer has them undone (BB-BOSS-DEFEAT). The simulator's answer has them
  undone already. When that boss wins the run, `win_game` pauses the game at the win screen
  (`G.SETTINGS.paused = true`) before the defeat's events run: until the player goes on in
  endless mode, the live game keeps showing the boss's debuffs.
- **`play` can answer before the round's total is set.** `play` waits for the round
  evaluation's first row and a `cash_out_button`. But `cash_out` leaves the button's UIBox in
  `G.I.UIBOX` (it is a minor of `G.round_eval`, not a child), so from a run's second round on
  the old button is found at once, and `play` answers before the last row sets
  `G.GAME.current_round.dollars` (`common_events.lua:1087`). A `cash_out` sent at once pays
  the previous round's total. `LiveBackend` leaves `cash_out_wait` (1 s) between the
  previous answer and a `cash_out`; the lockstep reconciles the money if it happens anyway
  (BB-CASHOUT-RACE). A player can't cash out before the button is up, and the simulator
  pays the round's own total.
- **`screenshot`** always fails with `Failed to encode screenshot` (nothing is drawn).
- **`add`** (debug) keeps the behaviour the test fixtures' setups were built with ([B03](live#b03)):
  a joker's `'edi'..ante` poll runs even when an edition is given (live skips it); a playing card
  draws no `'front'..ante` card (live draws one); an enhanced playing card isn't checked against
  the boss (live debuffs it at once). Stickers are forced as `force_stickers` does: eternal and
  perishable together, on any joker. A voucher `add` puts in the shop has no buy button live, so
  buying it raises in `buy.lua`; the simulator reports the same Lua error (`INTERNAL_ERROR`).
- **`rearrange`** also writes the new positions into `ability.order` and the shared
  `config.center.order` live; no rule reads them during a run, and the simulator doesn't.
- **Test endpoints** (`--debug`) are BalatroBot's `test_endpoint`, `test_state_endpoint`,
  `test_error_endpoint` and `test_validation`, with their exact responses.

## How it is checked

- `tests/bot/test_error_table.py`: every error message in the vendored endpoints (94 sites, one
  per `message =` or per value of a message variable) is produced by a test row with its exact
  name, code and message, or listed as unreachable with the reason (13).
- `tests/bot/test_upstream_suite.py`: BalatroBot's own endpoint tests run against
  `jackdaw serve` (455 pass; 6 strict xfails in `tests/bot/upstream_xfail.json`: described text
  fields and screenshots).
- `tests/bot/test_view_schema.py`: views from random runs fit `openrpc.json`'s `GameState`
  schema, patched where the schema is wrong (`tests/bot/schema.py`).
- `tests/bot/test_bot_native.py`: every engine tape is replayed through the requests; each step's
  snapshot equals the native step's (the sort mode aside, as above).
- `tests/parity/test_rust_setup.py`: the parity setups (`add`, `set`, `force_boss`) give the
  snapshots the Python engine gave, frozen in `tests/fixtures/setup_boards.json`.

Steamodded behaviour (`SMODS.add_card`, `SMODS.add_booster_to_shop`, `SMODS_BOOSTER_OPENED`) was
read from Steamodded 1.0.0~BETA-1503a as installed with BalatroBot and from the Lovely dump of the
patched game; none of it is vendored.

---
layout: default
title: Python API
---

# The Python API

The game engine is written in Rust (`crates/jackdaw-core`) and runs in-process through the
`jackdaw._core` extension. `jackdaw.core` is its Python face. It reproduces Balatro 1.0.1o
exactly, down to the RNG: it was ported function by function from the game's Lua source, checked
step by step against a Python reference engine (whose results are frozen in the test fixtures),
against LuaJIT itself for the RNG and the hand evaluation, and in lockstep against the live game
([Lockstep against the live game](live)).

For reinforcement learning, start with the [RL Project Guide](rl-guide): the environments wrap
this API. Use `jackdaw.core` directly for scripting, analysis, search, or your own environment.

## A run

```python
from jackdaw.core import Game
from jackdaw.engine.actions import SelectBlind, PlayHand, Discard, CashOut, BuyCard, NextRound

game = Game.new("b_red", stake=1, seed="TUTORIAL")   # back key, stake 1-8, seed
game.step(SelectBlind())                              # the round starts, the hand is dealt
game.step(PlayHand(card_indices=(0, 2, 3)))           # hand indices
print(game.phase, game.chips, game.hands_left)
```

- **Creating a run.** `Game.new(back, stake, seed=None, challenge=None)`. Without a seed it
  draws one the way the game does. For a challenge, pass its id (`"c_omelette_1"`); the back is
  then the challenge deck.
- **Stepping.** `step(action)` takes an action dataclass from `jackdaw.engine.actions`, or its
  tape form (`["PlayHand", [0, 2, 3]]`), and plays until the game waits for the next decision.
- **Errors.** An action the rules refuse raises `IllegalActionError`, and the run is unchanged.
  `NotPortedError` would mean a missing rule; nothing raises it now that every rule is ported.

The actions are `SelectBlind`, `SkipBlind`, `RerollBoss`, `PlayHand`, `Discard`, `SortHand`,
`SwapHandLeft`/`Right`, `SwapJokersLeft`/`Right`, `CashOut`, `BuyCard`, `BuyAndUse`,
`SellCard`, `UseConsumable`, `RedeemVoucher`, `OpenBooster`, `PickPackCard`, `SkipPack`,
`Reroll` and `NextRound`.

## What is legal

```python
for action in game.legal_actions():
    print(action)
```

- **Order.** `legal_actions()` lists the actions in a fixed order.
- **Plays and discards.** `PlayHand` and `Discard` appear once each, with no cards, standing
  for any selection of 1-5 hand cards (Cerulean Bell's forced card must be included).
- **Consumables.** A consumable that targets cards carries a default selection.
- **Checking one action.** `game.check(action)` returns why the rules refuse an action, or
  `None`, without changing the run.

`legal_actions(Legality.BALATROBOT)` keeps only what the live
[BalatroBot](balatrobot) also executes. Use it for agents that will play the real game. It
drops sim-only actions such as `RerollBoss` and `BuyAndUse`, and moves the bot refuses.

## Reading the run

Scalars are properties: `phase`, `seed`, `ante`, `round`, `dollars`, `chips`, `hands_left`,
`discards_left`, `won`. Areas and the rest are read-only views:

| Property | Type |
|---|---|
| `hand`, `jokers`, `consumables`, `deck`, `discard_pile` | `tuple[CardView, ...]` |
| `shop_jokers`, `shop_vouchers`, `shop_boosters`, `pack_cards` | `tuple[CardView, ...]` |
| `blind` | `BlindView` (`key`, `chips` to beat, `dollars`, `boss`, `disabled`) or `None` |
| `hand_levels` | mapping hand name → `HandLevel` (`level`, `chips`, `mult`, `played`, `visible`) |
| `tags` | held tag keys |
| `last_score` | `Score` (`hand_type`, `chips`, `mult`, `total`, `dollars`, `debuffed`) or `None` |

A `CardView` has:
- `key` (the center: `"j_joker"`, `"c_fool"`, `"m_glass"`, `"c_base"`...);
- for playing cards, `front` (`"H_A"`), `suit` and `rank`;
- `edition`, `seal`, `debuff` and `face_down`;
- `cost` and `sell_cost`;
- the stickers;
- a read-only `ability`.

Views are frozen: they describe the run when they were read.

## Exact previews and search

```python
score = game.preview_play((0, 1, 2, 3, 4))   # the real play on a copy
print(score.hand_type, score.total)

branch = game.clone()                        # an independent copy, well under a microsecond
branch.step(Discard(card_indices=(5, 6, 7)))
```

`preview_play` runs the actual step on a copy, so it includes every joker, enhancement, edition,
seal, the boss and the RNG. The run itself is unchanged. `clone()` is cheap enough for tree
search. `scoring_cards(positions)` gives the hand those cards make and which of them would score
(`("Pair", [1, 3])`), without playing them.

## How a hand scored

```python
game.record_scoring = True
game.step(PlayHand(card_indices=(0, 1, 2, 3, 4)))
play = game.last_play                  # a Play; None after a step that played no hand
print(play.hand, play.level, play.score.total)
for e in play.events:
    print(e.kind, e.card, e.target, e.chips, e.mult, e.x_mult, e.hand_chips, e.hand_mult)
```

With `record_scoring` on, each play records how it scored, in the order `G.FUNCS.evaluate_play`
shows it. A `Play` has:
- `hand`, and its `level` when played (before any level-up);
- `played` and `scoring`, the cards' sort ids in play order;
- `events`;
- `score`, a `Score`.

Each `ScoreEvent` has a `kind`, the `card` it belongs to (where the game shows it) and its
`target` when that's another card. It records what changed: `chips` and `mult` added, `x_mult`
multiplied, `dollars` paid. It also carries the hand's chips and mult after it (`hand_chips`,
`hand_mult`), so the last event's pair is the score's.

| `kind` | What happened |
|---|---|
| `level_up` | a joker levelled the hand up before it scored (Space Joker): the new `level` and base |
| `hand` | scoring starts: the hand's base chips and mult at `level` |
| `blind` | the boss changed them (The Flint) |
| `card` | a scoring card's own chips, mult, x mult or money (enhancements, Gold Seal) |
| `held` | a held card's bonus (Steel Card) |
| `edition` | an edition's bonus, on a scoring card, a joker or a consumable |
| `joker` | a joker's effect, on `target` when it acts on a card |
| `retrigger` | `target` scores again, or counts again in hand: `card` is the Red Seal's card or the joker |
| `debuffed` | a scoring card the boss debuffs, which adds nothing |
| `not_allowed` | the boss doesn't allow the hand: it scores nothing |
| `plasma` | Plasma Deck balanced the chips and mult |
| `destroyed` | a scoring card destroyed after the hand: a Glass Card that `shattered`, or Sixth Sense's 6 |

Recording is off by default and changes nothing: the run, its snapshot and hash, the observations
and the masks are the same either way.

## Building a state

```python
from jackdaw.core import GameBuilder

game = (
    GameBuilder("b_red", stake=2, seed="DEMO0001")
    .boss("bl_hook")
    .select_blind()
    .joker("j_blueprint")
    .joker("j_joker", edition="polychrome")
    .card("H_A", enhancement="m_glass", seal="Red")   # into the hand during a round
    .money(50)
    .build()
)
```

The additions go through the same operations as BalatroBot's debug commands `add` and `set`
(`Game.debug_add`, `Game.debug_set`, `Game.debug_restock_shop`).

## Saving and comparing runs

- `to_dict()` returns the canonical snapshot (`jackdaw.snapshot/1`,
  [schema](snapshot-schema)). It is plain JSON-compatible data and is also the save format;
  `Game.from_dict(snapshot)` restores it exactly.
- `state_hash()` is the SHA-256 digest of the canonical snapshot. Equal states have equal hashes.
- `replace_state(snapshot)` loads an edited snapshot into the run at the same decision point,
  keeping what a snapshot doesn't carry (the card-area settings BalatroBot's view reports, the
  hand's highlights). The live lockstep uses it to copy live values into its shadow run.

## BalatroBot

- `bot_view()` returns BalatroBot v1.5.2's `gamestate` view of the run, as the live bot would
  send it, except that text fields carry names.
- `bot_request(action)` returns the `(method, params)` request that performs an action live, or
  `None` for a sim-only action.
- `jackdaw serve` runs a BalatroBot-compatible JSON-RPC server on the simulator.
- `jackdaw.bridge.LiveAdapter` plays the live game in lockstep with a `Game` as its shadow, and
  `jackdaw lockstep` does it at scale: see [Lockstep against the live game](live).

See [BalatroBot on the simulator](balatrobot).

## Observations

`observation_buffer()` returns the RL observation (encoder v1) as raw float32 data, and
`jackdaw.env.encode_observation(game)` wraps it as an `Observation`; `jackdaw.env.get_action_mask(game)`
gives the action mask. The environments in `jackdaw.env` (`BalatroEnvironment`,
`BalatroGymnasiumEnv`, `BalatroVectorEnv`) build on these; see the [RL Project Guide](rl-guide).

## Where the source doesn't decide

A few things the Lua source leaves open, and the engine's choices:

- **`pairs()` over the poker hands.** To Do List's hand, the Orbital Tag's hand and The Ox's
  tie-break follow the order `pairs(G.GAME.hands)` visits the hands in, which Lua doesn't
  define. The engine uses the order the game's own LuaJIT 2.0.5 gives (probed in its
  `lua51.dll`), confirmed against the live game.
- **Unseeded draws.** The first shop's Buffoon pack and the Charm and Meteor Tags' packs pick
  their `_1` or `_2` variant with an unseeded `math.random`. The variants hold the same cards; the
  engine always picks `_1`.
- **`unique_val`**, the last tie-break between two identical cards, is the creation order.
- **The profile.** Shop and pack pools leave out locked cards; the engine assumes a fully
  unlocked profile.
- **Where vanilla stops.** With two or more jokers, all debuffed, Crimson Heart's pick draws from
  an empty list and the game errors; the engine skips the pick. When the hand, the deck and the
  play area are all empty, vanilla queues `end_round` again every frame; the engine runs it once.

## Speed

On one core of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (Windows, MSVC release build):

| Operation | Time |
|---|---|
| A new run | 4 µs |
| `clone()` | 0.3 µs |
| A play, no jokers | 1.0 µs |
| A play with five jokers | 2.1 µs |
| Cash out and fill the shop | 2.2 µs |
| Opening a booster pack | 1.7 µs |
| A reroll | 1.1 µs |
| An RNG draw | 0.05 µs |

`cargo test --release -p jackdaw-core --test perf -- --ignored --nocapture` prints these.

The environments step about 155,000 times a second (`BalatroEnvironment`) and 180,000 times a
second (`BalatroGymnasiumEnv`) on one core, and `BalatroVectorEnv` about 1.1 million times a
second on 8 threads (256 envs), counting the time inside the environment, not the policy's
(`uv run pytest -m benchmark`).
